question: Locate the anchor function for the exposure_digest field in the console.log object whose action is flag.exposure after typing the exposure user, choosing the flag, enabling send-exposure, and clicking Record Exposure on the page. The same exposure_digest value is also sent inside the body of a fetch POST request to the exposure endpoint issued on record. The anchor function is the first target-specific request-transform value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after delegated click routing, action routing, the exposure gate, exposure material collection with page-context snapshot, tuple input preparation, asynchronous scheduling and runtime config selection, its function body itself constructs the target observable exposure digest rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or writing the value to the console or fetch call. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, the final console sink, or the fetch call site. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.
anchor_definition_general: General rule for resolving ambiguity: a function is target-specific with respect to the observable described above if at least one statement in its body either constructs/binds the target value, writes the target field, or dispatches the target action — and removing that statement would break the observed target output under the prescribed interaction. A function is generic if it is a reusable utility (hash/encode/serialize/normalize/collect-features), a control-flow dispatcher (router/interceptor-pipeline/event-bus/scheduler), or a preparation routine (validate input/collect UI state/lifecycle hook) whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the unique target-specific function on the chain whose immediate caller is generic — equivalently, the shallowest target-specific function on the path from the trigger to the sink. Three situations commonly cause confusion: (1) If target-specific C is called by generic dispatcher B and calls generic utility D, the anchor is C, not B or D. (2) If generic A writes whatever callee B returns into the target field and B computes that value, the anchor is B. (3) If the target-specific statement is one branch inside a larger function F, F remains a valid anchor candidate.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example (different scenario, for illustration only): A delivery-tracking page emits courier.handoff_code after the courier taps Log Handoff. Chain: tap Log Handoff -> collect parcel rows (generic prep) -> snapshot depot context (generic prep) -> schedule via microtask (generic dispatcher) -> select depot variant config (generic prep) -> compose handoff envelope variant (ANCHOR) -> order envelope rows (nested helper) -> fold rows into code (nested helper) -> compute digest (core utility) -> queue push (generic helper) -> write courier.handoff_code -> send handoff request (wrapper/sink). The handoff envelope variant composer is the anchor because its immediate caller is the generic config selector and its body explains why handoff_code is produced. Apply the same reasoning to this exposure reporter page and bundle.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice (the name immediately after the `function` keyword). Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends (exclusive).

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with `function <function_name>(` and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.
function_name and slice.code must refer to the same function declaration in the captured bundle.
slice.code must be one complete function (balanced braces), not a signature fragment, partial body, or multiple functions.
Return one top-1 function, not a list of candidate chains.
Do not return the final console sink or the fetch call site.
Do not return a generic DOM reader, version reader, formatter, router or transport helper when a more target-specific exposure digest value constructor is present.
Constrain the observable by both action and field.
Ignore console.debug and console.info decoy objects unless they feed the requested console.log object.

The target value is a 16-character ex_-prefixed exposure digest and should not be confused with shadow_exposure, assign_ref, audit_ref or non-target flag.assign/flag.audit exposure_digest-like decoys.
